checks: The ARM64 graphical terminal booted under QEMU and accepted the WinZBuf launch command.
The active graphical terminal installed its draw callback while the demo waited for input.
The demo drew the colored window z-buffer map; the top-left terminal region changed by more than 500 pixels and contained more than 1,000 green map pixels.
Escape returned to the graphical terminal, which evaluated 40+2; as 42.
scope_note: Automated QEMU ISO runtime evidence only. The demo's source draws its instruction in black on the terminal's black background, so acceptance verifies the colored z-buffer map rather than the instruction text. This does not establish live UTM or Raspberry Pi behavior.
